questions&answers.question: What kind of projects are you looking to work on?
questions&answers.answer: I'm mostly drawn to web projects that have a strong focus on user experience and creative design. I enjoy projects where there's room to think about both how something looks and how it works — whether that's a portfolio, a web app, or something more experimental.

questions&answers.question: Do you only do web or are you open to other types of projects?
questions&answers.answer: Primarily web, but I'm open to other types of projects too — especially anything that involves UI/UX or visual design. I also have experience with video editing, so if that's ever relevant I'm happy to bring it in.

questions&answers.question: What inspires your design decisions?
questions&answers.answer: A lot of it comes from browsing Pinterest and just saving things that catch my eye — textures, layouts, small details. I tend to gravitate toward designs that feel personal and intentional rather than flashy for the sake of it.

questions&answers.question: What does your typical project process look like from start to finish?
questions&answers.answer: I usually start by gathering inspiration and getting a feel for the direction before touching any code. From there I move into Figma to sketch out the idea, then build it out iteratively — adjusting as I go based on how things actually feel in the browser.

questions&answers.question: How do you balance creativity with functionality in your work?
questions&answers.answer: For me functionality always comes first — if something looks great but is confusing to use, it's not working. I try to find creative solutions within those constraints rather than sacrificing usability for aesthetics.

questions&answers.question: Do you work better solo or as part of a team?
questions&answers.answer: Both, honestly. I'm comfortable working independently and taking ownership of a project, but I also enjoy collaborating — especially when it means bouncing ideas off someone else early in the process.

questions&answers.question: Are you open to collaborating with other students or creatives?
questions&answers.answer: Definitely. I think some of the most interesting work happens when people with different skills or perspectives work together, so I'm always open to it.

questions&answers.question: Have you worked with clients before?
questions&answers.answer: Definitely. I think some of the most interesting work happens when people with different skills or perspectives work together, so I'm always open to it.

questions&answers.question: Do you take on small or passion projects?
questions&answers.answer: Yes, and honestly those are sometimes the most fun. Small projects are a great way to try something new or experiment without the pressure of a full brief.

questions&answers.question: What's something you're currently learning or improving on?
questions&answers.answer: Right now I'm getting more comfortable with React and Next.js — this portfolio is actually built with both, so it's been a hands-on way to learn. I'm also trying to get better at writing cleaner, more structured code overall.
